body:
WHAT
The self-verify rung is an OVERDRIVE-only end-of-turn round where the model must answer `DONE` or keep working. Its closing clause depends on whether the turn changed code: with no code change it says to judge only against the query and never invent verification rituals; with changed source files it names them and says 'fully handled' includes being settled — observed against the real thing (not merely compiled, re-read, reasoned about, or agreed with by a self-written stand-in) or an honest statement of what could not be run.

WHY
One fixed text cannot fit both turns: on a conversational turn a demanded build is waste, while on a code-changing turn warning against rituals gives the model licence to skip verification.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/finishing.ts — SELF_VERIFY prompt (id finishing.self-verify, placeholder {{closing}}), SELF_VERIFY_CLOSING_CODE, SELF_VERIFY_CLOSING_PLAIN, selfVerifyText(changedCode) (returns undefined when the rendered prompt is blank). Fired from engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — runTurn() `verify` computed when stopReason end_turn, !selfVerifyFired, totalToolCallsThisTurn > 0 and this.overdrive; isSelfVerifyDone().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. selfVerifyText([]) contains 'never invent verification rituals (builds, tests)' and does not contain 'You changed code this turn'.
2. selfVerifyText(['src/a.ts']) contains 'You changed code this turn (src/a.ts)', 'not merely compiled, re-read, reasoned about, or agreed with by a stand-in', and does not contain 'never invent verification rituals'.
3. Both variants keep the shared head: 'Internal self-check', 'output exactly this literal ASCII word … DONE'.
4. In an OVERDRIVE FakeProvider session where the turn made a Write of src/a.ts plus a Bash call and then end_turn, the pushed self-verify message uses the code closing; in a turn with a Read tool call only, it uses the plain closing.
5. With OVERDRIVE off, or with zero tool calls in the turn, no self-verify message is pushed at all.
